lints.name: authenticated_security_definer_function_executable
lints.title: Signed-In Users Can Execute SECURITY DEFINER Function
lints.description: Detects `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that are callable by signed-in users. Revoke `EXECUTE`, switch the function to `SECURITY INVOKER`, or move it out of your exposed API schema if signed-in users should not call it.

findings.detail: Function `public.current_person_id()` can be executed by the `authenticated` role as a `SECURITY DEFINER` function via `/rest/v1/rpc/current_person_id`. Revoke `EXECUTE` or switch it to `SECURITY INVOKER` if that is not intentional.

Function `public.has_role(required_role text)` can be executed by the `authenticated` role as a `SECURITY DEFINER` function via `/rest/v1/rpc/has_role`. Revoke `EXECUTE` or switch it to `SECURITY INVOKER` if that is not intentional.

Function `public.is_any_platform_admin()` can be executed by the `authenticated` role as a `SECURITY DEFINER` function via `/rest/v1/rpc/is_any_platform_admin`. Revoke `EXECUTE` or switch it to `SECURITY INVOKER` if that is not intentional.

Function `public.is_platform_super_admin()` can be executed by the `authenticated` role as a `SECURITY DEFINER` function via `/rest/v1/rpc/is_platform_super_admin`. Revoke `EXECUTE` or switch it to `SECURITY INVOKER` if that is not intentional.
